candidates.attacker_control: The JSON request body of `POST /actuator/gateway/routes/{id}` is deserialized directly into `RouteDefinition` (`@RequestBody`); each `FilterDefinition`/`PredicateDefinition` carries an attacker-chosen `name` (must match a registered factory) and an attacker-chosen `Map<String,String> args`, including values such as `#{...}`. `POST /actuator/gateway/refresh` is available on the same endpoint to force route conversion and thus evaluation.
candidates.counterevidence_checked: Checked that (a) `validateRouteDefinition` really only compares filter/predicate names against the registered factories and never inspects `getArgs()` (lines 147-175); (b) the `#{` branch in `getValue` is trivially satisfiable and is the only place route args are interpreted; (c) `ConfigurationService` has no guard/flag excluding actuator-supplied definitions; (d) `GatewayAutoConfiguration` registers the endpoints unconditionally when actuator is present and the endpoint is enabled (lines 819-843), with the in-memory repository as the default `RouteDefinitionRepository` (203-206); (e) SpEL in shortcut args is a legitimate feature for trusted file/YAML configuration, which is why the flaw is specifically the untrusted actuator write path combined with the privileged evaluation context; (f) the same codebase uses the restricted `SimpleEvaluationContext` in `DiscoveryClientRouteDefinitionLocator` (line 75), showing a safer pattern exists; (g) accessibility depends on actuator exposure, which limits real-world reachability but does not change the code-level defect.
candidates.impact: When the endpoint is exposed and unauthenticated, an attacker obtains SpEL evaluation with bean resolution and default type resolution: `@bean.method(...)` calls on arbitrary Spring beans and `T(...)`-style class access (e.g. Runtime/ProcessBuilder) can lead to execution of arbitrary code with the gateway process privileges, plus full route manipulation (traffic hijack, SSRF to internal services, credential-bearing request redirection). The same endpoint combination (write route + refresh) also enables persistence of malicious routes for the lifetime of the process.
candidates.prerequisites: 1) Spring Boot Actuator on the classpath (endpoint class is only registered `@ConditionalOnClass(Health.class)`); 2) the gateway actuator endpoint enabled and exposed over HTTP, e.g. `management.endpoints.web.exposure.include` contains `gateway` or `*` (the sample app `spring-cloud-gateway-sample/src/main/resources/application.yml` uses `*`); 3) the actuator web endpoints are reachable without effective authentication/authorization (or the attacker holds access to them). Default Boot exposure is health-only, so stock deployments without explicit exposure are not reachable.
candidates.root_cause: `ShortcutConfigurable.getValue` treats any filter/predicate argument beginning with `#{` and ending with `}` as a SpEL expression and evaluates it in a `StandardEvaluationContext` that has a `BeanFactoryResolver` set, giving access to `@bean` references, `T(...)` type references and arbitrary method invocation. The Gateway actuator endpoint accepts a full `RouteDefinition` from an HTTP client and its only validation (`AbstractGatewayControllerEndpoint.validateRouteDefinition`) restricts the filter/predicate *names* to registered factories; arguments are passed through untouched and later evaluated when routes are loaded. There is no allow-listing/sanitization of args, and no restricted evaluation context (contrast: `DiscoveryClientRouteDefinitionLocator` uses `SimpleEvaluationContext.forReadOnlyDataBinding().withInstanceMethods()` for the same kind of property expressions).
candidates.title: SpEL injection in route definitions written via the Gateway Actuator endpoint (args evaluated with StandardEvaluationContext + BeanFactoryResolver)
candidates.trace: POST /actuator/gateway/routes/{id} -> AbstractGatewayControllerEndpoint.save (lines 134-145) -> validateRouteDefinition (147-159, name-only check) -> RouteDefinitionWriter/InMemoryRouteDefinitionRepository.save (38-46) -> attacker triggers POST /actuator/gateway/refresh (94-98) -> RefreshRoutesEvent -> CachingRouteLocator.onApplicationEvent (79-90) -> RouteDefinitionRouteLocator.getRoutes/convertToRoute (94-120) -> loadGatewayFilters (123-164) / lookup (199-220) -> ConfigurationService.with(factory).properties(definition.getArgs()).bind() -> ConfigurableBuilder.normalizeProperties (ConfigurationService 137-144) -> ShortcutConfigurable.ShortcutType.normalize (86-143) -> ShortcutConfigurable.getValue (49-66): since the value starts with `#{` and ends with `}`, `parser.parseExpression(entryValue, new TemplateParserContext()).getValue(StandardEvaluationContext with BeanFactoryResolver)` evaluates it in the gateway JVM.
candidates.unverified: No code was executed, no scanner/SAST oracle was used, and no deployment was tested, so runtime exploitability and the actual actuator exposure/auth posture of any real application are unverified. Index relations are syntactic navigation candidates only (no data/control-flow proof). Also unverified: whether a later 3.0.x/3.1.x fix (if applied to a downstream build) would remove this path; the reviewed source itself contains no mitigation.
candidates.weakness_type: Expression Language Injection (SpEL) leading to remote code execution (CWE-917 / CWE-94)

coverage_summary: Reviewed the assigned 219-file snapshot (Spring Cloud Gateway 3.0.6, no test sources present). Deep-read the Gateway server actuator endpoints, route layer (RouteDefinition, InMemoryRouteDefinitionRepository, CachingRouteLocator, RouteDefinitionRouteLocator, Composite locators), support layer (ConfigurationService, ShortcutConfigurable, AbstractConfigurable, Configurable), filter/predicate factory base types and a sample of concrete factories and filters (AddResponseHeader, RewritePath, RequestHeaderToRequestUri, RedisRateLimiter, NettyRoutingFilter, rate limiter), plus the discovery locator and X-Forwarded resolver; skimmed the mvc/webflux ProxyExchange configuration classes pending full review. P1 relation index covered 217/219 files and 189 Java files with syntax-level symbols/edges; its own qualification states no data-flow, no control-flow, no semantic resolution, and no sast/oracle findings, and 2 source files are missing from the index. No runtime execution, tests, or scanners were run.
limitations: No runtime or test execution; all conclusions are static and source-text based, and no exploit payload was executed (per review constraints).

Reachability of the actuator endpoint depends on deployment configuration (exposure and authentication) that is not present in this repository; only the bundled sample shows `management.endpoints.web.exposure.include: '*'`.

The P1 index is syntactic only (no control/data-flow, no semantic resolution) and omits 2 source files from indexing; navigation edges were treated as leads and verified against source text but cannot prove runtime behavior.

The snapshot contains no test sources, so no repository tests could be checked for expected/patched behavior; whether a downstream build applies a later security patch cannot be determined from this tree.
The spring-cloud-gateway-mvc and webflux ProxyExchange classes (largest remaining unreviewed files) were only partially inspected; no conclusion is drawn about them.
Kotlin DSL sources (RouteDsl.kt) and documentation asciidoc files are largely absent from the snapshot scope and were not reviewed for security-relevant defaults.

rejected_leads.lead: RequestHeaderToRequestUriGatewayFilterFactory lets a request header (e.g. Host-like header) override the outbound request URI, enabling SSRF.
rejected_leads.reason: The header-driven URI override is the documented purpose of the filter and only takes effect when an operator explicitly adds it to a route; no default route uses it, and there is no trust-boundary crossing in this source snapshot by itself.

rejected_leads.lead: XForwardedRemoteAddressResolver.trustAll() / RemoteAddrRoutePredicateFactory trust spoofable X-Forwarded-For values, allowing client-IP spoofing.
rejected_leads.reason: Opt-in configuration; the source's own Javadoc explicitly documents the spoofing risk and directs users to maxTrustedIndex() instead. Not reachable with default configuration.

rejected_leads.lead: Actuator route-write endpoint allows arbitrary route URIs, enabling SSRF/traffic hijack by design.
rejected_leads.reason: Same root area and prerequisites as the submitted SpEL issue (exposed actuator endpoint); it is a consequence of the same trust-boundary problem rather than a distinct stronger root cause, so it was folded into the single candidate instead of being listed separately.

rejected_leads.lead: Missing @Valid on the actuator `@RequestBody RouteDefinition`, so bean-validation constraints (@NotEmpty predicates, @NotNull uri) are not enforced.
rejected_leads.reason: Robustness/input-validation gap only; no direct security impact demonstrated without an additional sink, and the SpEL path already covers the dangerous consequence.

rejected_leads.lead: RewritePathGatewayFilterFactory uses String.replaceAll with an operator-configured regex and $-substitution handling.
rejected_leads.reason: Regex and replacement come from trusted route configuration, not from request data; no attacker-controlled regex/replacement, so no demonstrated injection or ReDoS.

rejected_leads.lead: RedisRateLimiter builds Redis keys from a possibly request-derived keyResolver value.
rejected_leads.reason: Values are passed as Redis key/script arguments, not concatenated into Lua source; no script injection, and per-request key growth is expected behavior.

rejected_leads.lead: spring-cloud-gateway-mvc / webflux ProxyExchange forwards request headers when building proxy calls.
rejected_leads.reason: Only partially inspected; it exposes `sensitive`/`autoForward` header configuration and is a developer-facing helper, with no concrete attacker-controlled path verified in this review.
Information exposure depends on actuator exposure and authentication configuration (same precondition as the primary finding) and is lower impact; not selected.

summary: Spring Cloud Gateway 3.0.6 snapshot. The strongest source-evidenced issue is a SpEL-injection/RCE path reachable through the Gateway Actuator endpoint: `POST /actuator/gateway/routes/{id}` stores an attacker-supplied `RouteDefinition`, and when routes are converted (`POST /actuator/gateway/refresh`), filter/predicate `args` are bound through `ConfigurationService` -> `ShortcutConfigurable.getValue`, which evaluates any `#{...}` value with a `StandardEvaluationContext` carrying a `BeanFactoryResolver` (bean lookup) and the default type locator (`T(...)`). The endpoint's `validateRouteDefinition` only checks filter/predicate *names*, so SpEL embedded in the args of a legitimate filter (e.g. `AddResponseHeader`) is accepted. Exploitation requires the actuator gateway endpoint to be exposed and reachable (e.g. `management.endpoints.web.exposure.include=gateway`/`*` and no effective auth on the actuator), which is a deployment precondition rather than the default; the bundled sample app exposes `*`. No runtime verification was performed; the finding is based on fully traced source.
